title: Tuga A8 vs Tuga A10: 8 Inch or 10 Inch Rugged Android Tablet?
description: Tuga A8 (£379) or Tuga A10 (£449)? £70 apart. The A8 is brighter with a removable battery; the A10 has the 10.1 inch Full HD screen, IP68 and MIL-STD-810H.
summary: £70 apart, both 8000mAh: the A8 is far brighter at 1000 nits against 350 and its battery is removable; the A10 has the 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen, 8GB of RAM, Android 14, IP68 and MIL-STD-810H.
lede: For sole traders and small firms choosing between the two Android tablets in the range. The short answer: the A8 at £379 for outdoor work in direct sun and long shifts on a spare battery, the A10 at £449 for drawings, plans, spreadsheets and the tougher listed ratings.
verdict: Buy the Tuga A10 at £449 if you read drawings and plans on it or want the stronger listed ratings; buy the Tuga A8 at £379 if it works in direct sun or you want to swap batteries. The gap is £70. Both have 128GB of storage, an 8000mAh battery, dual SIM 4G and NFC. The £70 buys a bigger, sharper screen (10.1 inches at 1920 x 1200 against 8 inches at 1280 x 800), 8GB of RAM against 6GB, Android 14 against Android 12, IP68 against IP67, MIL-STD-810H, which the A8 does not list, and a listed operating range of -20°C to 60°C, where the A8 lists none.

Pay the £70 if you read drawings, plans or spreadsheets on the tablet, or want the ratings in writing. On an 8 inch screen a large drawing needs more panning and zooming than on 10.1 inches. The A10's newer Android version also counts if your apps need a recent release, so check them on the device. Both can take the paid 3-Year Warranty at £65. It is the tablet for a site cabin or a desk dock, where its 350 nit screen is less of a drawback: in direct sun on an open site, a roof or a dashboard mount, the A10 is much harder to read than the A8. The construction page goes through where it earns its place for drawings.

Keep the £70 if the tablet lives outdoors or on long shifts. The A8's 1000 nit screen is nearly three times the A10's 350 nits, and its 8000mAh battery is removable, so a charged spare takes over without stopping, which the A10 does not list. It has VESA mount points and pogo pin contacts for the Vehicle Mounting Dock, and its 8 inch size suits one hand up a ladder or a van door pocket. The A8 lists no weight, drop rating or MIL-STD rating, so if those numbers matter to you, they are on the A10. For forms, photos, route maps and quotes, the A8 is the cheaper choice, and the field service page covers where the A8 fits against the A6 and W8. If one job decides it, tell us what you do and we will say which we would buy.
chooseA: You read the screen in direct sun on roofs, open sites or a van dashboard: 1000 nits against the A10's 350.
You want to swap batteries rather than stop to charge: the A8's 8000mAh battery is removable, which the A10 does not list.
You want it on the dashboard: the A8 has VESA mount points, and the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) is listed for both tablets.
You hold it in one hand up a ladder or drop it in a van door pocket: 8 inches against 10.1.
Forms, photos and route maps are the job, and £70 is better kept in the business.
chooseB: You read drawings, PDF plans or full spreadsheets on the tablet, and check your own viewer apps run: 10.1 inches at 1920 x 1200 against 8 inches at 1280 x 800.
You want the tougher listed ratings: IP68 against the A8's IP67, plus MIL-STD-810H and a -20°C to 60°C operating range, neither of which the A8 lists.
You want the newer operating system and more memory: Android 14 and 8GB of RAM against Android 12 and 6GB.
The tablet lives in a site cabin or on a desk dock, out of direct sun: the Charging Dock (£49.99) is listed for the A10 and not the A8.
You store a lot of photos, plans or offline maps on the device: microSD up to 2TB, where the A8 lists a microSD slot without a figure.

faq.q: Is the Tuga A10 worth £70 more than the Tuga A8?
faq.a: For drawings and plans, or if you want IP68 and MIL-STD-810H in writing, yes; for forms, photos and route maps in the open, the A8 does the job for £70 less. The A10 costs £449 and the A8 £379. The £70 buys a 10.1 inch 1920 x 1200 screen in place of 8 inches at 1280 x 800, 8GB of RAM against 6GB, Android 14 against Android 12, IP68 against IP67, MIL-STD-810H and a microSD slot rated to 2TB. It gives up brightness (350 nits against 1000) and the removable battery. If you spend the day in PDF plans, BIM viewers or spreadsheets, pay it and buy the Tuga A10. If you work outdoors, fill in forms, take photos and follow routes, buy the Tuga A8 and keep the £70. Buying several? Device discounts run from 3 percent at two to 10 percent at ten or more, see bulk orders.

faq.q: Can I read the Tuga A10 screen outdoors?
faq.a: It is 350 nits and not listed as sunlight readable, so direct sun is much harder work than on the A8, which is 1000 nits and listed as sunlight readable. Indoors or in a site cabin it is the better screen for plans: sharper at 1920 x 1200 against the A8's 1280 x 800, and bigger at 10.1 inches against 8. If most of your day is on open sites or roofs, choose the A8, or keep the A10 for the cabin and the desk dock. The construction page says the same thing with the trades spelled out.

faq.q: Which lasts longer on a charge, the A8 or the A10?
faq.a: We cannot say. Both have an 8000mAh battery, but neither lists a run time in hours and the two have different screens and processors, so we will not guess. The difference is that the A8's battery is removable, so a charged spare can take over on a long day, and the A10 does not list a removable battery. The A10 lists quick charge without a figure; the A8 lists no fast charging. Both take the 12V DC Car Charger (£26), the Vehicle Mounting Dock (£109) has a DC power input, and the Charging Dock (£49.99) is listed for the A10 only, all on the accessories page. The A10 is rated to work from -20°C to 60°C; the A8 lists no operating temperature. Our guide to rugged tablets in winter covers what the cold does to any battery.

faq.q: Are the A8 and A10 the same size and weight?
faq.a: No, the A10 is the bigger tablet: 250 x 167mm, 14.5mm thick and 680g. The A8 does not list dimensions or a weight, so we will not give you a figure, but with an 8 inch screen against 10.1 it is the one for one hand and a van door pocket. If you need a figure for a case or a mount, ask us. The same Vehicle Mounting Dock, Hand Strap and Rugged Carry Case (fits tablets up to 10.1 inches) are listed for both; the Charging Dock is listed for the A10 only.
